column1: # Requirements for Mica::Encoding (milestones I1 and I3 of the iconv plan): the
# WHATWG Encoding Standard (https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/, pinned at commit
# 7d2e3e08e1), Unicode chapter 3's maximal-subpart rule, the iconv-compatible
# names Crystal programs use, and the conversion limits.

column3: Every label resolves to its encoding after ASCII whitespace trimming and ASCII case folding; anything else resolves to nothing
A label longer than 64 bytes is refused before lookup
The iconv-compatible rule keeps iconv's meanings (exact ISO-8859-1, UTF-16 and UTF-32 with byte order marks, UCS-2, BIG5-HKSCS) and refuses the replacement encoding's labels
Every entry of every index decodes from its bytes to its code point
Every code point with an index pointer encodes to the bytes of the pointer the standard's encoder chooses
Ill-formed UTF-8 is replaced per maximal subpart (Table 3-8)
UTF-16BE and UTF-16LE decode surrogate pairs and replace unpaired surrogates and a trailing odd byte
Every single-byte encoding decodes and encodes through its index
gb18030, GBK, Big5, EUC-JP, ISO-2022-JP, Shift_JIS and EUC-KR decode and encode as the standard's algorithms do
Fatal stops with the problem's kind and offset, replacement writes U+FFFD or a character reference, skip drops
After a fatal error the converter returns to its initial state
Output is the same for every split of the input into chunks and every output buffer size, in every error mode
Output never exceeds the encoding's documented worst-case growth
Converting into a caller's buffers allocates nothing per call beyond the result
Every vector file is verified against its pinned sha256 before use, and a mismatch names the file
